full_judgment:
9. Learned District Judge in reversing the judgment of the learned Assistant Judge held that the plaintiffs of both the suits claimed title on plot No. 2918 under Jote No. 237 recorded in Jamabandi Khatian No. 1230/55 but in the Revisional Settlement Khatain there is no mention of the said plot and the plot No. 265 of revisional khatian No. 956 has been described as Government khas land and the same had been recorded in MRR and BS Khatian in the name of Cox's Bazar Airport. Learned District Judge further held that the plaintiff in the plaint did not even state the date of alleged settlement in favour of Abul Khair nor did file any rent-receipts in support of the said settlement and, as such, the acquisition of title by Abul Khair on the basis of alleged settlement remained disproved. Learned District Judge further found that the certified copy showing the Bandabasta Khatian in the name of Abul Khair is nothing but a forged and created document and Abul Khair''s acquisition of title followed by possession could not be proved. Learned District Judge finally found that the plaintiff of both the suits did not acquire any title and possession over the suit land. 

 14. It is admitted that the disputed 0.20 acre of land is within the land of defendant-Airport Authority measuring 137.32 acres of land which was a khas land. The defendant Airport Authority claimed to have acquired ownership and possession. On the basis of a transfer made by the Government to the Civil Aviation Department in Miscellaneous Case No. 5 of 1957-58 and the entire land had been recorded in the name of Defendant-Airport Authority in MRR and BS Khatians. It is the case of the plaintiff that the British Army took possession of the suit land along with other lands during the Second Great War and after the Great War Abul Khair took over possession of the said land and also got compensation for the damage caused to the house constructed by him on the suit land but no papers had been produced before the court below to show that after the Second Great War Abul Khair took possession over the disputed land and got compensation for the damaged house. In the absence of legal evidence it is difficult to hold that Abul Khair went into possession over the suit land on the basis of settlement from the Government. Learned Trial Judge based his decision on discussion of factum of possession of the plaintiff ignoring the vital aspect that the plaintiff failed to produce any document showing settlement from the Government in his favour. 

 16. In the case of Prahalad Chandra Mahato and others vs. The State of Bihar and others reported in AIR 1976 Patna 109 as referred to by Mr Abul Kalam Azad the fact is that the plaintiffs filed a suit for declaration that the tank with its embankment, the homestead and khas property of the plaintiffs and the proforma defendants No. 6-10 have no title to the suit property and their recognition as tenants by the state is illegal. There was also a further prayer for permanent injunction restraining the defendants from interfering with the possession of the plaintiffs. The suit was contested by the defendant Nos. 1-5 who were State of Bihar and its officers. The trial Court dismissed the suit with the finding that the plaintiffs were never in possession of the disputed property and appeal was preferred by all the plaintiffs and the lower appellate Court dismissed the suit with the finding that the entire tank vested in the Government and modified the decree of the trial Court to the effect that the defendant Nos. 6-10 got no right in the disputed property as the same vested in the State of Bihar. Thereafter, second appeal has been preferred by the defendant Nos. 6-10. The second appeal was allowed. The judgment and decree of the appellate Court in so far as it interfered with the decree passed by the trial Court which was in favour of the defendant-appellant Nos. 6-10 were set aside and those of the trial Court restored. In the said case all the plaintiffs preferred an appeal as because the suit was dismissed. But in this instant case plaintiff's suit was decreed and against that added defendant No. 3 preferred an appeal being aggrieved by the decree passed by the trial Court. So, the facts and circumstances of the cited case are quite distinguishable and got no manner of application in the facts and circumstances of this present case.
